clue.text: Erstwhile condition of property that's left

definitions.meaning: in older English the word meant one's state or standing in life
everything a dead person leaves behind, their possessions and land

explanation.definitionFit: Archaically the word meant state or rank, and today it names the assets a deceased person bequeaths.

clue.text: Carrier of notes for the personnel

definitions.meaning: the five ruled lines on which music is written

explanation.definitionFit: A musical stave carries notes, and an organisation's workforce is its employees collectively.

clue.text: Upper-class Asian lad tortured in Spain

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A posh young Asian man is mistreated while in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' rearranges U plus ASIAN and LAD. The definition is a place 'in Spain', the southern region whose capital is Seville.
explanation.definitionFit: The region lies in the south of the Iberian kingdom, a province within that country.

clue.text: Oriental flower festival

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as something that flows towards the east
the Christian spring feast of the Resurrection

explanation.definitionFit: A thing flowing eastward could jokingly be called this, and it is also the spring Christian holiday.

clue.text: Formula to quote in a novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone wants a standard form of words for citing a passage in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being quoted; it is the anagram signal, rearranging QUOTE IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a formula is an expression stating that two quantities are equal.

clue.text: It's mainly operated for the benefit of the retired

definitions.text: It's mainly operated for the benefit of the retired

parts.words: It's mainly operated for the benefit of the retired
parts.note: mainly means run off the mains electricity supply, and the retired are not pensioners but people who have gone to bed

explanation.definitionFit: A heated bedcover powered from the mains warms those who have turned in for the night.

clue.text: Pen this and there's one more to go

definitions.text: Pen this and there's one more to go

parts.words: Pen this and there's one more to go
parts.note: put the letters PEN in front of this word and you get the word for second to last

explanation.definitionFit: The word means last or final; with the prefix 'pen' it means next to last, leaving one more.

clue.text: Language of many in rear of plane

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the tail is the back end of an aircraft
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Many people speak some tongue at the back of the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside TAIL. The language is spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dravidian tongue spoken by tens of millions in south India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Concerned with smelling cutting of old plant

indicators.note: cutting of means the word old is trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at a cutting taken from an aged plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks horticultural beside 'cutting', but it is an industrial works; 'cutting of' trims OLD to OL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the sense of smell, as in the nerves serving the nose.

clue.text: We see tin fall, glowing with heat

parts.note: a can is a tin container
a descent is a fall

explanation.surface: Watching molten tin drop, we see it glowing hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We see' only introduces the scene. The answer is the rarer root of 'incandescent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means shining with heat, white-hot.

clue.text: Drop catch, not surprisingly, wearing this

definitions.meaning: to fumble or miss a catch, as in cricket
someone with hands in a fur hand-warmer would naturally fail to hold the ball

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bungle a catch, and the noun is a fur tube for warming hands, which makes catching hard.

clue.text: Notes flowing, making one wealthy

parts.note: A and F are two musical notes
fluent means flowing smoothly

explanation.surface: Music that flows freely is making one rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making one' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people with plenty of money, rich.

clue.text: Ill-will of many a chess-board heroine

parts.note: M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
Lewis Carroll's heroine crosses a chessboard in Through the Looking-Glass

explanation.surface: Lots of hostility directed at a heroine on a chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Carroll's Alice becomes a pawn that is queened in the sequel to Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and the wish to harm someone are the same thing as ill-will.

clue.text: Tree for father in America, or Java

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: US is short for the United States
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Looking for a tree for Dad, whether in America or Java.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or Java' points to the tree's home: it is the Javanese poison tree of travellers' legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A Javanese tree whose sap was used as an arrow poison, named after the Malay word for poison.

clue.text: Examination of virtual description of certain politics

definitions.meaning: a hands-on test, as in a science exam
politics concerned with what can really be done, in effect rather than in theory

explanation.definitionFit: A practical is a hands-on test, and 'practical politics' is the realistic art of the possible.

clue.text: Bury one or more inside

parts.note: to inter is to bury
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to bury one person, or several, within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more' looks part of 'one or more', but 'more inside' is the definition: the Latin word is a comparative meaning inner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin the word is a comparative of 'inward', meaning further within.

clue.text: Revolt about telephone man' upset no one

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word no and the letter for one are turned upside down

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An uprising about the inventor of the telephone has upset nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NO plus I to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising against authority is a revolt.

clue.text: Train chap, or old-time road driver

parts.note: to coach is to train
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man who trains others, or someone who drove carriages long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Before railways, the driver of a horse-drawn coach on the highway.

clue.text: The Underground late here?

parts.note: late means dead, not delayed; the dead lie in this underground burial place

explanation.definitionFit: An underground cemetery of tunnels and recesses where the dead are laid.

clue.text: Cries like a hound or horses

definitions.meaning: howls deeply as a hunting dog does

explanation.definitionFit: A hound howls in this way, and the same word names reddish-brown horses.

clue.text: It secures the joints of a sea-bird, some say

indicators.note: some say means the word is how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a skua is a predatory gull-like sea-bird

explanation.surface: A gadget holds together the cuts of meat from a sea-bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech SKUA and SKEWER sound alike. 'joints' are cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pin is pushed through meat to hold it together while roasting.

clue.text: Non-active part of guest at ice-show

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An idle part played by a guest at an ice-show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless or unchanging is not moving.

clue.text: Where Raleigh wrote, with difficulty, his world history

definitions.text: Where Raleigh wrote, with difficulty, his world history

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests struggling, so the letters of the word are shuffled

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Raleigh laboured over his History of the World while imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges WROTE. Raleigh wrote his History of the World while imprisoned in the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of London held Raleigh for thirteen years, during which he wrote his history.

clue.text: Mid-Balkan class of goods, like caustic soda

indicators.note: Mid takes the inner letters of the word Balkan, dropping its first and last

parts.note: a line is a range of products

explanation.surface: Some kind of goods from the central Balkans resembling caustic soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium hydroxide is a strong base, so things resembling it are basic rather than acidic.

clue.text: Sound technical expertise? Not at all

indicators.note: Sound says the word is what one hears when it is spoken

parts.note: know-how is practical skill

explanation.surface: Is the technical expertise sound? Not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective praising the expertise; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect adverb meaning in no way whatever.

clue.text: Flat-bottomed boat from firm in Cornwall

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, SW
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A barge bought from a company based in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at the far south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a broad punt-like barge with a flat base.

clue.text: Keep hanging about, say, for the thirteenth loaf?

indicators.note: say means the phrase sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: to keep someone hanging about is to make them wait

explanation.surface: A baker keeps customers waiting for the extra loaf of a dozen.
explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen: the extra loaf was added to make up the weight, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra item added to bring a quantity up to full weight, like the baker's thirteenth.

clue.text: It's fashionable in wine, blow it!

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated with wine fashions exclaims 'Blow it!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow it!' looks like an oath; it says this is something you blow, a woodwind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-reed woodwind is played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Revives Military Intelligence

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
intelligence means information or news

explanation.surface: Military Intelligence is brought back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Military Intelligence' looks like one unit, the British spy service, but it splits in two; the Royal Engineers are a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore or refresh something is to bring it back to life.
